qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High switching costs in proprietary building management systems (Metasys) and installed-base services, alongside York industrial chillers for mission-critical data center cooling; supported by tangible operating ROIC > 20% and demonstrated pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Leading commercial HVAC and building automation provider fails Munger peace-of-mind balance sheet standards due to elevated leverage (long-term debt of $8.6B vs. FY25 net income of $1.7B, yielding LT debt / NI of ~5.1x vs. <=4.0x hurdle), persistent multi-year restructuring and separation expenses, negative tangible equity, and capital allocation prioritizing a $5.0B accelerated share repurchase over debt reduction. [5-10Y g: data center/commercial HVAC 4% + building services 3% + price 1% - restructuring drag -1%]
qualitative.evidence: Following the August 2025 close of the $8.1B sale ($5.0B net cash proceeds) of its Residential & Light Commercial HVAC unit to Bosch, Johnson Controls operates as a pure-play commercial building solutions provider with ~$23B in continuing revenue and solid operating margins (10-14%). However, 10-year GAAP ROIC has averaged 7-10% (median 9.2%) weighed down by $17B+ of goodwill and intangibles dating from the 2016 Tyco merger. Reported cash conversion has been repeatedly depressed by restructuring and separation costs. Balance sheet remains overleveraged with total debt of $9.9B ($8.6B long-term debt) against FY25 net income of $1.7B (LT debt / NI ~5.1x, exceeding the <=4.0x maximum). Management directed the $5.0B net proceeds from the Bosch sale into an accelerated share repurchase rather than deleveraging, failing Gate 6.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
